idea: Wei et al 2021 (cited Ch 7.5): for one intersection, reward = queue length; for networks, pressure (sum of incoming-lane queue minus outgoing-lane queue per movement) is equivalent to minimising global travel time. Simple state (lane queue + current phase) performs as well as complex states. Max-pressure picks the phase with the largest pressure, with min-green and amber/all-red kept safe.
does: A stdlib extension (signal_override hook) choosing the next phase by pressure computed from per-lane queues, usable as a baseline in run_experiment against Webster/SCATS/SCOOT.
inputs: per-approach and per-exit lane queue counts from the live Frame, phase-movement table, min/max green
outputs: phase choice each decision interval, delay/queue comparison vs fixed and adaptive plans
existing: partial: SCATS/SCOOT adaptive timing exist; actuated and max-pressure not built
notes: No equations given in the book, definition from Wei et al; classic Varaiya max-pressure is a few lines. Add to sources.md.

topic: Tabular Q-learning signal agent and action schemes
idea: Four action schemes for RL signal control: set phase duration; set split ratio of a fixed cycle; step to next phase in a cyclic sequence; choose any phase. Surrogate rewards (queue, wait, speed, throughput, switching frequency) used instead of delayed travel time. Weights are fragile, so use minimal terms.
does: Train a small tabular Q-learning controller (discretised queue bins x phase) headlessly across seeds inside run_experiment and report it against fixed-time and max-pressure; the LLM agent can also reason from the same four action schemes and queue reward.
inputs: network, demand, state bins, reward weights, episodes, seeds
outputs: learned policy table, learning curve, paired comparison vs baseline
notes: Stdlib only: tabular, not deep. Needs thousands of episodes so runs headless at CPU speed; amber/all-red must stay enforced.

topic: Bus holding control and headway CV reward
idea: Bus bunching: each bus on arrival at a stop holds d = a*T, a in [0,1], T max hold; reward = -(1-w)*CV^2 - w*a with CV^2 = Var[h]/E[h]^2 over forward/backward headways; state = passengers on board, forward headway, backward headway. Bunching is inherently unstable (Newell and Potts 1964).
does: Add a headway-regularity KPI (CV of headways per stop and route) to results, and a holding-control extension (hold at a stop in proportion to how short the forward headway is) that the assistant tests against no holding in run_experiment.
inputs: bus arrival times at stops from the simulation, max hold T, weight w
outputs: headway CV^2, bunching count, mean and max delay added by holding, comparison table
existing: partial: buses on a headway and TSP agents exist; no headway-variability KPI; passengers at stops not built
notes: Holding rule can be rule-based first (a = clip((h_target - h_forward)/h_target)); RL optional. Dwell with no passengers modelled means bunching arises only from signals and traffic, so the KPI is still useful for TSP evaluation.

idea: Learn or fit a car-following model so simulated spacing and speed track observed ones, with reward/error = log(S_sim/S_obs) and log(V_sim/V_obs); state (v, relative speed, spacing), acceleration clipped to +-3 m/s2, kinematic update V(t+1)=V(t)+aT, S(t+1)=S(t)+(Vrel(t)+Vrel(t+1))/2*T, T=0.1 s, restart from empirical data when an event ends.
does: Given observed leader-follower trajectories (CSV), grid-search or random-search Krauss parameters (tau, sigma, accel, decel) to minimise the log-ratio spacing/speed error through a replay of the leader, and report fitted parameters with the error.
inputs: leader speed series, follower observed gap and speed, parameter ranges
outputs: best-fit Krauss parameters, RMSE of spacing and speed, error by parameter
existing: none (calibration exists on counts and routes only)
notes: DDPG itself is deep RL and not feasible without numpy; only the problem setup (replay leader, error metric) is worth taking.

topic: Camera-free time-to-collision and near-crash rule; Heinrich ratio
idea: TTC = s/r where s is bounding-box height and r its growth rate (no camera parameters); double threshold 0<h/r_h<delta, 0<w/r_w<phi, delta<phi. Heinrich ratio 1 major injury : 29 minor : 300 no-injury events justifies counting near-crashes as surrogate safety data.
does: Count near-crash events in a run as TTC below a threshold with deceleration beyond a limit, per road/junction, and rank hotspots; optionally scale to a crash estimate by an explicitly labelled Heinrich-style ratio.
inputs: vehicle gaps and speeds per step, TTC threshold, hard-brake threshold
outputs: conflicts per veh-km per road, hotspot ranking, TTC distribution
existing: partial: rear-end conflicts are measured (crossing conflicts and PET not built)
notes: The vision part is irrelevant; in the simulator TTC = gap/closing speed is exact. The Heinrich scaling is contested, so state it as an assumption only.

idea: Unsupervised learning: k-means (K user-chosen, centroid by Euclidean distance) and PCA to group passengers or time series into behaviour classes (early birds, night owls...).
does: k-means (stdlib, a few dozen lines) on per-road or per-junction 24-hour flow/speed profiles or per-run KPI vectors to find road classes and regimes, and to pick representative days or seeds.
